headline: Britain EXPANDS military support for Saudi Arabia to 'defensive' air patrols by RAF jets
dek: UK expands to defensive RAF air patrols over Saudi; Egypt deploying air defense + aircraft (no ground troops); US rules out troops, offers logistics; Saudi envoy accuses Ansar Allah of exploiting crises/diverting ~1.34T riyals fuel revenue + $2B/yr smuggled oil.
sources: UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting (via AP); anonymous regional official on Egypt (via AP); US envoy Tom Barrack at Global Security Forum, Doha (via AP); Saudi Amb. to Yemen Mohammed Al-Jaber (X post, via Arab News/ajel.
fault_line: Defending Saudi civilians — or dragging London and Cairo into a wider regional war?

sections.what_happened: UK expands to defensive RAF air patrols over Saudi; Egypt deploying air defense + aircraft (no ground troops); US rules out troops, offers logistics; Saudi envoy accuses Ansar Allah of exploiting crises/diverting ~1.34T riyals fuel revenue + $2B/yr smuggled oil.
sections.what_verified: ToI AP version confirms UK RAF defensive patrols; bastillepost AP relay confirms Barrack + Egypt details; Arab News confirms Al-Jaber X statement; TOI liveblog: 'Egypt pledged support for Saudi Arabia'; judgenap digest (Oct 20): Egyptian National Defense Council pledged 'all possible forms of support'.
sections.what_disputed: Ansar Allah claims (via China Daily Monday): six attacks on Saudi oil/aviation targets over 48h in response to 200+ Saudi strikes; Ansar Allah figures unverifiable; the UK/Egypt moves are responses, scale of future commitment unclear.
sections.why_matters: The war widens: London and Cairo step onto Riyadh's shield while Washington says no boots — the Yemen front goes international.
sections.context: Background: Yemen/Saudi — NEW (Tuesday, AP): Britain EXPANDS military support for Saudi Arabia to 'defensive' air patrols by RAF jets (jets will shoot missiles/drones out of the air, NOT strike Ansar Allah targets on ground; UK had already offered in-air refueling); Egypt to deploy air-defense systems and aircraft to help repel missiles/drones fired toward Saudi Arabia, no ground troops in Yemen (anonymous regional official); US envoy Tom Barrack (Doha): US 'not prepared to deploy troops', will supply logistics; Saudi envoy Mohammed Al-Jaber (X, Tuesday): accused Ansar Allah of exploiting crises and diverting revenues to fund war

totw_analysis: Our read: The war widens: London and Cairo step onto Riyadh's shield while Washington says no boots — the Yemen front goes international. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Defending Saudi civilians — or dragging London and Cairo into a wider regional war?
related_short_title: 'Inconceivable' — Egypt Votes Today on Defending Saudi Arabia
